1.

By this award, I will dispose off the present claim filed by Workman, pursuant to reference under Section 10(1)(C) & 12(5) of Industrial Disputes Act, received from the office of Deputy Labour Commissioner (South-West), Labour Department, Govt.
of NCT of Delhi vide order reference no.
F.25(166)/R-52/SWD/Lab./214 dated 23.07.2025, whereby, the following issue has been referred to this Court for adjudication:-
"Whether the services of the Workman Sh. Satyavir Yadav S/o Sh. Naval Singh Yadav, aged-58 years, Mobile No. 987328943, Aadhar Card No. 667091901526 have been terminated illegally and/or unjustifiably by the Management; and if so, to what relief is he entitled and what directions are necessary in this respect?"
2. The aforesaid reference was received by this Court on 30.07.2025 and the statement of claim was thereafter filed by Workman on 24.09.2025.

Brief case of Workman, as per his statement of claim, is that he was working with Management, as a driver since 01.04.2022, against last drawn monthly wages of Rs. 13,000/- which were less than the minimum wages notified by the appropriate Government, however, Management had not issued any appointment letter in his name.

It is further his case that Management has failed to provide legal facilities, such as- Satyavir Yadav Vs. M/s Midfield Secondary School casual leave, minimum wages and festival leaves to Workman despite repeated demands of Workman and despite repeated assurances of Management.

sentences.text: 3. During the course of his employment, according to him, he availed medical leaves for the period 29.11.2024 to 04.12.2024.

When, after availing the aforesaid medical leaves, according to him, he again returned on his duty on 05.12.2024, Management did not allow him to resume his duty and on the same day, illegally terminated his services without any advance notice/notice pay or service compensation.

Management, according to him, has failed to reinstate him into the job despite the complaint and claim of Workman before Assistant Labour Commissioner, Hari Nagar, New Delhi and despite receipt of demand notice dated 14.12.2024 from Workman.
5. It is further his case that since the date of illegal termination of his services by Management, he is wholly unemployed, in as much as, he could not get any alternative job despite search.
Workman has thus prayed for his reinstatement with full back wages, continuity of service and all other consequential benefits.

sentences.text: Management appeared in response to notice of statement of claim and filed its written statement on 17.11.2025.

In its written statement, Management has categorically denied existence of any employer-employee relationship between the parties to present claim, while, alleging that Workman was neither engaged, nor, retained by Management on any contract or appointment, nor, was he ever on the pay roll of Management.

Under the aforesaid circumstances, according to Management,
there was no occasion Satyavir Yadav Vs. M/s Midfield Secondary School for Management to terminate his services, much less, illegally.

sentences.text: Management has thus prayed for dismissal of present claim of Workman with exemplary cost, while, simultaneously pointing- out an inordinate delay of about ten months on the part of Workman in raising the present dispute after the alleged illegal termination of his services.

7. No rejoinder to the aforesaid written statement was filed on behalf of Workman despite opportunity and hence, on the basis of pleadings of parties, following issues were settled by this Court vide order dated 17.11.2025:-
( i) Whether there existed relationship of employee and employer in between the parties to the present claim petition?

(OPW) 
(ii) Whether the services of the Workman have been terminated by the Management on 05.12.2024 illegally and/or unjustifiably?

(OPW) 
(iii) Relief, if any.

8. Workman has thereafter examined himself as WW-1 i.e. as the sole witness in support of his case and tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.WW1/A along with following documents:
(i) Ex.WW1/1: Copy of demand notice dated 14.12.2024.
(ii) Ex.WW1/2: Postal receipt regarding dispatch of aforesaid demand notice.

(iii) Ex. WW1/3: Copy of statement of claim filed by Workman before the Conciliation Officer, Hari Nagar.
9. WW-1 was duly cross-examined by Ld. AR of Management and during his cross-examination, he has produced a copy of Satyavir Yadav Vs. M/s Midfield Secondary School police clearance certificate dated 04.10.2024 Mark WW-1/4, purportedly issued by the Office of DCP, Special Branch, Delhi Police in the name of one Sh. Balraj S/o Sh. Chandan Singh.

11. Management has thereafter examined its Estate Manager namely Sh. Narender Kumar as MW-1 i.e. as the sole witness in support of its case.
He has tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.MW1/A besides, his authority letter Ex.MW1/1. MW-1 was duly cross-examined by Ld. AR for Workman.
No other witness was examined on behalf of Management despite opportunity and hence, on the submission of Ld. AR for Management, Management's evidence was closed vide order dated 12.12.2025.

Final arguments on behalf of both the parties were thereafter heard.
Besides, written arguments have also been filed on behalf of Management.

It is submitted by Ld. AR for Workman that Workman has been able to prove, not only, the existence of employer-employee relationship between the parties to present claim, but also, illegal termination of his services by Management on 05.12.2024 by way of his uncontroverted testimony in the form of affidavit Ex. WW1/A.

He submits that inability of Workman to produce any documentary evidence of his employment with Management was due to the reasons beyond his control, in as much as, no such document was ever issued by Management in the name of Workman.

He has thus prayed for an award in favour of Workman in terms of prayer made by Workman in his statement of claim, in as much as, according to him, Management has failed to prove that Workman had remained gainfully employed at any point of time after illegal termination of his services by Management.

13. On the other hand, it is submitted by Ld. AR for Management that despite burden to prove the existence of employer-employee relationship between the parties to present claim being upon Workman, Workman has failed to discharge the aforesaid onus, in as much as, he has not produced any document, such as- appointment letter, employment contract, wage slip, identity card,
attendance card, ESI/EPF slip or authorization letter, if any, issued by Management in his name authorizing him to drive the bus of Management to prove his employment with Management.
14.

On the contrary, according to him, Management has Satyavir Yadav Vs. M/s Midfield Secondary School produced the entire record in respect of its employees, pursuant to an application of Workman under Section 11(3)(b) of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, and in none of the aforesaid records, name of Workman was found mentioned as an employee of Management.

sentences.text: I have heard the submissions made on behalf of both the parties and have carefully perused the material available on record.

My issue-wise findings, on the issues settled by this Court vide order dated 17.11.2025, are as follows:-
Issue no. (i): Whether there existed relationship of employee and employer in between the parties to the present claim petition? (OPW)
17. Onus to prove the aforesaid issue was upon Workman.

As Satyavir Yadav Vs. M/s Midfield Secondary School has already observed herein above, in order to discharge the aforesaid onus,
Workman has examined himself as WW-1 i.e. as the sole witness in his evidence.

entities.text: Satyavir Yadav Vs. M/s Midfield Secondary School
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. WW-1/A, he has, once again, reaffirmed on Oath all the averments made by him in his statement of claim.

18. However, otherwise than by way of his self-serving statement to the aforesaid effect, Workman has failed to produce any document as a proof of his employment with Management since 01.04.2022 until 04.12.2024.

It is sought to be contended by Ld. AR of Workman that inability of Workman to produce any document as a proof of his employment with Management was due to the reason beyond his control, in as much as, no such document was ever issued by Management in the name of Workman.
19. I do not find any force in the aforesaid submission made on behalf of Workman.

No doubt,
admittedly, Management does not issue any appointment letter to any of its employees, however, it was categorically deposed by MW-1 during his cross- examination that the identity cards are being provided by Management to all its employees.
Workman has however failed to produce any identity card issued by Management in his name.

20. Moreover, it was deposed by Workman that during his employment with the Management,
Management had got his police verification conducted, however, he has failed to produce police clearance certificate, if any, issued in his name at the instance of Management.

Rather, a bare perusal of police clearance certificate dated 04.10.2024, produced by him during Satyavir Yadav Vs.
M/s Midfield Secondary School his cross-examination, shows that the same is not even in the name of Workman and it is in the name of one Sh. Balraj S/o Sh. Chandan Singh, another employee of management, whose name was found duly reflected in the record of employees of Management,
produced by MW-1 pursuant to an application of Workman under Section 11(3)(b) of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
21.

In fact, as has already been observed herein above, pursuant to an application of Workman under Section 11(3)(b) of Industrial Satyavir Yadav vs M/S Midfield Secondary School on 23 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54109499/
5 Disputes Act, 1947, Management has produced the entire record of its employees and admittedly the name of Workman did not figure, in the aforesaid record, as an employee of Management.

sentences.text:
22. The Court can also take judicial notice of the fact that as per Rule 7A of Delhi Motor Vehicle Rules, 1993, a permit holder of transport vehicle is required to submit a list of all the drivers hired by him together with their passport size photographs and other particulars to the Secretary,
Transport Department Government of Delhi and to notify any change in the said list within five days.
In fact, as per aforesaid Rule, no transport vehicle can ply in Delhi in the absence of any authorization card displayed thereon containing the name, photograph and other particulars of the driver.
Satyavir Yadav Vs.
M/s Midfield Secondary School 23.

The Workman, in the present case, was allegedly driving the bus of the Management School and hence, if there was any truth in his aforesaid plea, nothing stopped him from summoning the aforesaid record from the State Transport Authority.
Workman has however failed to take any steps to summon the record either qua aforesaid authorization card or the alleged Police Clearance Certificate in his name for reasons best known to him.
He has also failed to produce the proof of receipt of salary by him from Management, on the pretext, that Management used to pay his salary in cash.

24. Since the Workman has failed to produce or summon any documentary evidence of his employment with Management despite availability thereof, if there was any truth in his claim, and the record, produced by Management, in respect of its employees does not contain his name as an employee of Management, in my considered opinion, Court cannot record a finding on the aforesaid issue in favour of Workman, merely, on the basis of his self-serving statement to the aforesaid effect.
25. Issue no. (i) is thus decided against Workman.
Issue no. (ii): Whether the services of the Workman have been terminated by the Management on 05.12.2024 illegally and/or unjustifiably?

(OPW) 
26. Onus to prove the aforesaid issue was upon Workman.

In view of my finding on issue no. (i)
herein above, since, Workman has failed to prove that he had ever been in employment of Management, there was no occasion for Management to terminate his services on 05.12.2024 or on any other date, much less, illegally.
Satyavir Yadav Vs.
M / s Midfield Secondary School 27
. Issue no. (ii) is thus decided against Workman.
Issue no. (iii): Relief, if any.

Workman is not entitled to any relief.
29. Present claim of Workman against the Management is thus dismissed and reference dated 23.07.2025 is answered in negative in following terms:

"Workman Sh. Satyavir Yadav S/o Sh. Naval Singh Yadav, has failed to prove existence of any employee- employer relationship between parties to present claim or that his services were terminated by Management on 05.12.2024 either illegally or unjustifiably and hence he is not entitled to any relief."
